verdict: Healthpeak's revenue rose 16% to $821M as its Janus Living senior-housing business grew 78% after $1.75B of acquisitions, while heavy depreciation held GAAP earnings to $0.02 a share against $0.44 of adjusted FFO.

kpis.label: Revenue growth
kpis.note: Revenue was $821M, vs $706M a year ago

kpis.label: EPS (GAAP diluted)
kpis.note: vs a $0.17 loss a year ago

kpis.label: FFO as Adjusted per share
kpis.note: vs $0.46 a year ago — the REIT cash-earnings measure that adds back depreciation

kpis.label: Senior housing revenue
kpis.note: Up 78% YoY — Janus Living closed $1.75B of senior-housing acquisitions in the quarter

segments.name: Outpatient Medical
segments.note: Rent from medical office buildings — the largest business. Revenue slipped 2% after property sales, though same-store property profit (NOI) grew 3.1%.

segments.name: Senior Housing
segments.note: Resident fees and services at senior-housing communities run through Janus Living, the company's senior-housing REIT. Growth is mostly bought: $1.75B of communities were acquired in the quarter.

segments.name: Lab
segments.note: Rent from life-science laboratory buildings. Revenue up 5%; occupancy rose 130 basis points in the quarter and 270 since year-end.

segments.name: Other & interest income
segments.note: Loans, a preferred-equity investment, three other properties and interest income — a small remainder that shrank YoY.

opex.name: General & administrative
opex.note: Running the company — the only cost line shown below gross profit in this REIT presentation; property-level and financing costs sit in cost of revenue (see footer).

otherDetail: Other income of $9M plus $4M of equity income from joint ventures, less the $19M of profit that belongs to noncontrolling partners — outside owners who share in Janus Living and other joint ventures — for a net $7M cost. What remains is the $17M attributable to Healthpeak's own shareholders.
follow100Note: Kept-as-profit is the $17M attributable to Healthpeak shareholders; the rows add to $99.99 due to rounding.

takeaways.title: Senior housing is transforming the company
takeaways.text: Senior-housing revenue jumped 78% to $268M as Janus Living closed $1.75B of acquisitions in the quarter (with about $370M more after quarter-end). It is now a third of all revenue, up from a fifth a year ago — growth bought with acquisitions rather than won organically.

takeaways.title: Depreciation explains the tiny GAAP profit
takeaways.text: Depreciation and amortization of $299M — more than a third of revenue — is why GAAP EPS is just $0.02 while FFO as Adjusted, which adds depreciation back, is $0.44 a share. For landlords, the FFO figure is usually the more useful guide to cash earnings.

takeaways.title: The core medical portfolio shrank slightly
takeaways.text: Outpatient Medical revenue fell 2% to $315M after building sales, even though same-store property profit grew 3.1% and 846,000 square feet of leases were signed. Lab revenue rose 5% to $224M with occupancy up 270 basis points since year-end.

oneTimers: Transaction costs of $10M in the quarter ($43M in the first nine months), mostly tied to the Janus Living senior-housing acquisitions — they sit inside cost of revenue in this presentation.
footerNote: REIT presentation following the company's statement layout: cost of revenue is total costs and expenses excluding general & administrative — it combines property operating costs ($379M), depreciation & amortization ($299M), interest expense ($84M) and transaction costs ($10M), less a small impairment recovery. Net income is the $17M attributable to Healthpeak Properties, Inc. (total net income was $37M before the $19M belonging to noncontrolling partners). Segment revenues are from the Form 10-Q segment note; 'Other & interest income' combines $7M of non-reportable-segment revenue and $7M of interest income and other.
